newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares hesistant of Wall Street exuberance.
newsitem.headline: German shares hesistant of Wall Street exuberance.

text.p: German shares appeared modestly prepared to keep on following the gyrations of Wall Street in late trade on Wednesday and on Thursday despite the DAX showing tentative interest in further advances.
The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade on Wednesday up 55.62 points at 3,395.95 points but the DAX slipped to 3,384.01 points in post-bourse IBIS electronic dealings.

Traders noted the DAX rose only 1.70 percent on Wednesday and failed to keep pace with the 2.6 percent gain in the Dow Jones index on Tuesday, one of the index's most historic gains, despite the dollar trading above 1.71 marks in European trade.
Other factors weighing on the German market were worries about upcoming elections in France and Britain and their impact on the debate over the start of European currency union.

A drop in DAX heavyweight Siemens AG, the electronics group, also capped market interest. Siemens reported flat first-half results for its 1996/97 business year and gave a muted outlook for the balance of the year.
Siemens shares, among the most heavily-traded during the day, ended bourse trade down 2.30 marks at 88.90 marks.
"That was not enough to keep the market from keeping up," said one trader of Siemens.
"There's a general level of insecurity about the market's ability to keep going higher," the trader said.

Among other shares, preference shares in haircare products group Wella AG ended up 75 marks at 1,030 marks as Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said it had raised its recommendation in the stock to "overweight" from "neutral".
Wella said on Tuesday it expected 1997 net profits to climb 25 percent, with sales up seven percent.
Airline Lufthansa ended up 90 pfennigs at 23.,80 marks as dealers cited strong technical factors and a positive mood surrounding its restructuring plan to boost operating profits.
